title: Event Times and Time-Varying Markers
text: Inside sim_effect() expression, event_time(proc, k) time process proc’s k-th event, 0 hasn’t happened yet. negative k counts back latest event: event_time(visit, -1) latest visit event_time(visit, -3) third latest. Combined current time t, gives effects time since event: t - event_time(operation, 1) time since first operation. Since event_time() 0 event, t - event_time(operation, 1) just t someone yet operated. Multiplying event count, operation * f(t - event_time(operation, 1)), can used effect event happened. Suppose patients may undergo operation, raises death hazard immediately , gradually fades . example look like : \lambda_{\text{death}}(t)   = \lambda_0(t) \exp\left( 3 \cdot \text{operation}(t) \cdot e^{-2(t-T_{\text{operation},1})} \right). baseline hazards constant (\nu = 1), \lambda_0(t) = 0.02. operation, measured time since operation, u = t - T_{\text{operation},1}, death hazard therefore h(u) = 0.02 \exp\left( 3 e^{-2u} \right). Right operation hazard h(0) = 0.02 e^3 \approx 0.40, 20 times baseline. time passes, e^{-2u} goes 0 hazard returns baseline 0.02. Two time units operation, 6% baseline. check simulation, follow operated patient operation death censoring. Nelson–Aalen estimator estimates cumulative death hazard since operation, (substituting w = 3 e^{-2v}, dv = -dw / (2w)) \begin{aligned}     H(u) & = \int_0^u h(v) \, dv     = 0.02 \int_{3 e^{-2u}}^{3} \frac{e^w}{2w} \, dw \\          & = 0.01 \left[ \operatorname{Ei}(3) - \operatorname{Ei}\left( 3 e^{-2u} \right) \right],   \end{aligned} \operatorname{Ei}(x) = \int_{-\infty}^x e^w / w \, dw exponential integral. Censoring end follow-don’t depend time since operation, estimate unbiased. , H(u) computed numerical integration.  shapes follow pattern. expression times coef added log-hazard, example:
code: operation_model <- sim_model(   censoring = sim_process("censoring", eta = 0.05, nu = 1),   operation = sim_process("transient", eta = 0.2, nu = 1, limit = 1),   death = sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.02, nu = 1),   effects = list(     sim_effect(       death ~ operation * exp(-2 * (t - event_time(operation, 1))),       coef = 3     )   ) )  operation_data <- sim_events(   operation_model,   n = 5000,   max_cens = 10,   seed = 1 ) head(operation_data) #> Key: <id> #>       id       time     event operation #>    <int>      <num>    <fctr>     <num> #> 1:     1  4.9115104 censoring         0 #> 2:     2  3.6612164 operation         1 #> 3:     2 10.0000000  max_cens         1 #> 4:     3  2.0634278 operation         1 #> 5:     3  6.4647265     death         1 #> 6:     4  0.3566003 operation         1 operation_time <- operation_data[event == "operation", .(id, T_op = time)] post_op <- merge(   operation_data[, .SD[.N], by = id],   operation_time,   by = "id" ) post_op[, u := time - T_op]  fit <- survfit(Surv(u, event == "death") ~ 1, data = post_op)  H <- function(u) {   vapply(     u,     function(x) integrate(function(v) 0.02 * exp(3 * exp(-2 * v)), 0, x)$value,     numeric(1)   ) } u_grid <- seq(0, 8, length.out = 200)  ggplot() +   geom_step(aes(fit$time, fit$cumhaz, colour = "Nelson–Aalen")) +   geom_line(aes(u_grid, H(u_grid), colour = "True H(u)"), linetype = "dashed") +   coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 8)) +   labs(     x = "Time since operation",     y = "Cumulative death hazard",     colour = NULL   )

text: sim_covariate() drawn baseline never changes. sim_mark() drawn baseline redrawn time one update processes fires, staying constant . takes: init: function N (earlier covariates) giving baseline values, sim_covariate(). update: transient processes whose events redraw marker. draw: function N lp giving new values. new value depends specified sim_effect()s marker. update, coef * terms summed linear predictor lp, draw can use, e.g. mean rnorm(). effects can use anything hazard effect can, including marker’s value update, see triggering event happened. marker can also used sim_effect() like covariate, hazards always use current value. Suppose patients blood pressure measured visits. High blood pressure makes treatment initiation likely, treatment lowers subsequent blood pressure, blood pressure treatment affect stroke hazard. Blood pressure therefore time-varying confounder effect treatment stroke. Let’s define setup, new measurement depends previous one treatment: \text{bp}_{\text{new}}   \sim N\left( 130 + 0.8 (\text{bp}_{\text{prev}} - 130) - 2 \cdot \text{treatment}, \; 6^2 \right). Untreated, blood pressure mean 130. Treatment lowers new measurement mean 2, since measurement carries 0.8 previous one’s deviation, effect converges mean 130 - 2 / (1 - 0.8) = 120. summary unrolls effects marker updates: bp[k+1], value k+1-th visit, drawn bp[k] current treatment status. data, bp value row’s event, bp_0 baseline value. Refit from "observed" data, then rebuild a sim_model(), as if # observed_model were unknown: fits <- list(   censoring = coxph(     Surv(time, event == "censoring") ~ L0 + A0,     data = observed_data   ),   cause1 = coxph(Surv(time, event == "cause1") ~ L0 + A0, data = observed_data),   cause2 = coxph(Surv(time, event == "cause2") ~ L0 + A0, data = observed_data) ) types <- c(censoring = "censoring", cause1 = "terminal", cause2 = "terminal")  model <- sim_model_from_fits(fits, observed_data, types) model #> <sim_model> #>   2 covariate(s): L0, A0 #>   3 process(es): censoring, cause1, cause2 #>   6 effect(s): #>     censoring ~ 0.4875836 * L0 #>     censoring ~ -0.9133865 * A0 #>     cause1 ~ -0.4906536 * L0 #>     cause1 ~ 0.3575318 * A0 #>     cause2 ~ 0.02845469 * L0 #>     cause2 ~ 0.6609588 * A0 new_data <- sim_events(model, n = 1000) head(new_data) #> Key: <id> #>       id     time     event        L0    A0 #>    <int>    <num>    <fctr>     <num> <num> #> 1:     1 1.620870 censoring 0.9559121     0 #> 2:     2 2.219986    cause2 0.9885974     1 #> 3:     3 2.006563    cause2 0.4766994     1 #> 4:     4 1.701406    cause1 0.1054270     0 #> 5:     5 1.036467    cause2 0.5620987     1 #> 6:     6 4.455880    cause2 0.1166055     1  # code: library(survival)  # Some "observed" data, from a 3-cause competing-risks sim_model(): set.seed(1405) observed_model <- sim_model(   L0 = sim_covariate(function(N) runif(N)),   A0 = sim_covariate(function(N, L0) rbinom(N, 1, plogis(-0.5 + L0))),   censoring = sim_process("censoring", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),   cause1 = sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),   cause2 = sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.1, nu = 1.1),   effects = list(     sim_effect(censoring ~ L0, coef = 0.5),     sim_effect(censoring ~ A0, coef = -1),     sim_effect(cause1 ~ L0, coef = -0.5),     sim_effect(cause1 ~ A0, coef = 0.5),     sim_effect(cause2 ~ A0, coef = 0.5)   ) ) observed_data <- sim_events(observed_model, n = 1000)  # Refit each process from that "observed" data, then rebuild a sim_model() # from the fits, as if observed_data came from an outside source and # observed_model were unknown: fits <- list(   censoring = coxph(     Surv(time, event == "censoring") ~ L0 + A0,     data = observed_data   ),   cause1 = coxph(Surv(time, event == "cause1") ~ L0 + A0, data = observed_data),   cause2 = coxph(Surv(time, event == "cause2") ~ L0 + A0, data = observed_data) ) types <- c(censoring = "censoring", cause1 = "terminal", cause2 = "terminal")  model <- sim_model_from_fits(fits, observed_data, types) new_data <- sim_events(model, n = 1000) head(new_data) #> Key: <id> #>       id     time     event        L0    A0 #>    <int>    <num>    <fctr>     <num> <num> #> 1:     1 1.512868    cause2 0.9559121     1 #> 2:     2 2.208823    cause2 0.9885974     0 #> 3:     3 2.047464    cause2 0.4766994     1 #> 4:     4 1.677063 censoring 0.1054270     0 #> 5:     5 1.145823    cause1 0.5620987     0 #> 6:     6 4.629326    cause1 0.1166055     1  # Event-type distribution should be comparable between the observed and # newly simulated data (a few simulated individuals reach the end of the # observed follow-up, as "max_cens"): event_levels <- levels(new_data$event) rbind(   observed = prop.table(table(factor(observed_data$event, event_levels))),   simulated = prop.table(table(new_data$event)) ) #>           censoring cause1 cause2 max_cens #> observed      0.269  0.336  0.395    0.000 #> simulated     0.277  0.328  0.393    0.002
